title: Meyhane Etiquette for First-Timers: Ordering, Pacing & Splitting Bills
seoTitle: Istanbul Meyhane Etiquette: Ordering, Pacing & Bills
metaDescription: Master Istanbul meyhane etiquette: why dinner lasts 3–4 hours, how to order rakı (tek, duble, bottle), classic vs yeni nesil venues, and fish pricing.
quickAnswer: A traditional Istanbul meyhane evening is structured around unhurried conversation over three to four hours, moving from cold meze and white cheese to warm ara sıcak plates, grilled meat or fish, and seasonal fruit. Order rakı by the glass (tek or duble) or bottle (35cl or 70cl), and always confirm off-menu fish prices per kilogram before ordering.

body.text: Knowing basic istanbul meyhane etiquette turns a potentially confusing night of trays, glassware, and shared plates into one of the most relaxed meals in Türkiye.
Why is a Turkish meyhane dinner meant to last 3–4 unhurried hours?

A Turkish meyhane dinner lasts three to four hours because the evening is designed around conversation (muhabbet) rather than turning tables. As outlined in [GoTürkiye's Istanbul Meyhane Culture Guide](https://goturkiye.com/istanbul/meyhane-culture), food arrives in deliberate waves—cold meze first, then warm starters, followed by a modest main course and fruit—so diners pace both eating and drinking comfortably.

Nobody orders a main course in the first five minutes. A waiter brings a cold meze tray (tepsi) or invites you to the glass counter to pick four to six shared plates. Warm starters (ara sıcak) like calamari or paçanga böreği arrive an hour later, well before grilled fish or köfte.
How do you order rakı by the glass (tek/duble) vs bottle (35cl/70cl)?

Order rakı as a tek (single pour, roughly 4–5cl) or duble (double pour, roughly 8–10cl) if only one or two people are drinking lightly. For two or more regular drinkers staying the full evening, ordering a 35cl (otuz beşlik) or 70cl (yetmişlik) bottle is more economical and comes with chilled water, ice buckets, and fresh glasses.
Here is how the table ritual works once your rakı arrives:

items: Water and Ice: Pour rakı first, then cold water (1:1 or 1:2) so it turns milky (aslan sütü). Add ice last so anise oils do not crystallize.
Separate Water Glass: Keep two glasses side by side—one for diluted rakı, one for plain water—sipping alternately.
Clinking Glasses: Toast (Şerefe!) by clinking the base of your glass with eye contact. Never top up someone's glass unasked.
Non-Alcoholic Options: Şalgam suyu (fermented purple carrot juice, mild or spicy) and sparkling mineral water (soda) are classic pairings.

body.text: What is the difference between classic historic meyhanes and modern "yeni nesil" meyhanes?

Classic historic meyhanes focus on quiet conversation, low-key Turkish classical music (fasıl or background recordings), and timeless seasonal meze at neighborhood institutions like [Yakup 2 in Asmalımescit](https://www.yakup2.com.tr/tarihimiz.php). Modern "yeni nesil" (new generation) meyhanes shift from a seated dinner into a loud, DJ-led party with 1990s Turkish pop, fixed menus, and dancing between tables.

body.text: As local dining guide [Meyhanedeyiz](https://meyhanedeyiz.biz/temalar/yeni-nesil) notes, yeni nesil venues start as dinner and quickly turn into hands-in-the-air nightlife. Decide whether your group wants to talk or dance before choosing your neighborhood.
Should you check prices before ordering fresh fish off-menu?

Yes—always ask the waiter for the exact price per kilogram (kilo fiyatı) and the estimated weight of any fresh seasonal fish before it hits the grill. Under [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Trade price-label rules updated in January 2026](https://ticaret.gov.tr/haberler/ticaret-bakanligi-tarafindan-fiyat-etiketi-yonetmeliginde-degisiklik-yapildi), restaurants must display clear menus at entrances and tables, yet daily-catch fish is still priced by weight.

Wild Bosphorus lüfer (bluefish), kalkan (turbot), or levrek (sea bass) cost far more than farmed fillets. Per the [Ministry of Trade Consumer Information Guide](https://tuketici.ticaret.gov.tr/yayinlar/tuketici-bilgi-rehberi/fiyat-etiketleri-hakkinda-bilgilendirme), venues also cannot add undisclosed cover charges absent from their displayed price list.

items: Confirm whether the venue serves a la carte or a fixed menu when booking.
Start with white cheese (beyaz peynir) and melon (kavun) plus 4–5 cold meze before ordering hot dishes.
Ask "Kilosu ne kadar?" (How much per kilo?) and check the fish on the scale for off-menu seafood.
Expect Alman usulü (splitting evenly) among friends; ask for itemized card splits before the waiter prints the final check.
Budget a 10% tip in cash or confirm whether a service charge (servis ücreti) is already printed on the menu.

faq.q: Can you go to a meyhane if you do not drink rakı or alcohol?
faq.a: Yes. Meyhanes welcome guests who drink wine, beer, şalgam suyu, or mineral water. Nobody is pressured to order rakı, though ordering a good spread of meze is expected.

faq.q: What is the right number of cold meze for two people?
faq.a: Two diners typically start with four to five cold meze plates plus bread, white cheese, and melon, then add one or two warm starters (ara sıcak) an hour later.

faq.q: How do locals split the bill at a Turkish meyhane?
faq.a: Groups of friends usually divide the total evenly (hesabı bölüşmek) because almost every plate and bottle is shared across the center of the table.

faq.q: Do Istanbul meyhanes require advance reservations?
faq.a: For Friday and Saturday nights, yes—historic Beyoğlu, Karaköy, and Kadıköy meyhanes often fill up days ahead. Midweek tables are easier to book a day in advance.

faq.q: What does "kuver" mean on a Turkish restaurant bill?
faq.a: Kuver is a per-person table cover charge covering bread, water, butter, or table service. Under Turkish trade regulations, any cover or service fee must be clearly listed on the menu beforehand.

faq.q: What should you eat at the end of a meyhane night?
faq.a: Classic meyhanes finish with chilled seasonal fruit (meyve tabağı)—often quince, figs, or melon—followed by Turkish coffee rather than heavy syrupy desserts.
